Electronic warfare is emerging as a decisive force in modern military operations, with technologies such as artificial intelligence, cognitive electronic warfare, quantum sensing and photonics set to strengthen India’s indigenous defence capabilities and strategic autonomy, said M. Sheik Althaf, Outstanding Scientist and director of the Electronics and Radar Development Establishment (LRDE), on Wednesday.
Addressing the 65th annual day celebrations of the Defence Electronics Research Laboratory (DLRL), a premier DRDO laboratory in Hyderabad, he said advances in electronic warfare were crucial to realising the vision of Atmanirbhar Bharat and reducing dependence on imported defence technologies.
DRDO Director General (Electronics and Communication Systems) and Outstanding Scientist B.K. Das said indigenously developed systems offer significant cost advantages over imported alternatives while giving the country greater control over maintenance, upgrades and long-term support.
Describing DLRL as an “architect of silent warfare”, he emphasised the need to empower Indian industry and encourage greater participation in developing next-generation defence technologies. DLRL director K. Murali outlined the laboratory’s achievements and progress in electronic warfare systems during 2026. Scientist Tapas Kumar Hazra also spoke.
A video tracing DLRL’s 65-year journey, key milestones and indigenous technology developments was screened at the event. Staff members who completed 20 years of service were felicitated with mementoes and certificates, according to a press release.
